forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Sevenoaks projects £250k deficit as service costs rise and reserves drain
news_drafts.lead: Sevenoaks Council is forecasting a £250,000 deficit for the year to March 2027, a material shift from its break-even budget after four months of the financial year. Service spending has overrun by £244,000, with particular pressure in planning and regulatory services, partly offset by strong investment returns of £165,000. The council's usable reserves, money set aside for planned spending, have been drawn down by £841,000 in the first four months alone, with the Financial Plan Reserve depleted by 18 per cent. At the current rate, total reserves would fall by approximately £2.5 million over a full year. The deficit includes the impact of a 3.3 per cent pay award still under negotiation, estimated to cost £71,000 beyond budget. The council's treasury management, including investments in multi-asset income funds and a housing loan portfolio, is performing well but cannot fully offset the underlying operational pressures.

findings.headline: Building Control facing both fee income decline and rising costs
findings.detail: Building Control has shown unfavorable variances due to lower than budgeted fee income and overspends on additional costs of staff and contractors.
findings.matters: Services under dual pressure—declining fee income coupled with rising staffing costs—signal deeper service sustainability concerns
findings.quote: Unfavourable variances were seen in Building Control due to lower than budgeted fee income and overspends due to additional costs of staff and contractors.

findings.headline: Waste transition generating £100,000 favorable variance from vacant posts
findings.detail: Waste transition has shown a £100,000 favorable variance as a result of underspends on core salary budgets due to vacancies.
findings.matters: Savings from unfilled posts are typically temporary and not sustainable as vacancies are subsequently filled, making this a one-off rather than structural improvement
findings.quote: Waste transition had also shown a favourable variance of £100,000 as a result of underspends on core salary budgets due to vacancies.

findings.headline: Car park and market income declined due to operator struggles at Sunday markets and competition from privately owned car park at Bradbourne
findings.detail: Sunday market income has been lost due to operator struggles, partially offset by inflation income from Wednesday markets. Car park day ticket income at Bradbourne is down because of competition from a privately owned car park. The current market contract expires in March 2027.
findings.matters: Discretionary income under competitive pressure and subject to external operator decisions indicates revenue vulnerability; contract expiry in March creates an upcoming decision point
findings.quote: Markets had underperformed due to loss of income on Sunday markets due to operator struggles. Carpark income was down due to loss of day ticket income at Bradbourne car park, due to competition from a privately owned carpark.

findings.headline: Investment strategy generating £165,000 favorable variance
findings.detail: The council's Investment Strategy continues to perform well, with a mix of longer-term multi-asset income funds and shorter-term money market investments creating a £165,000 favorable variance.
findings.matters: Investment income is material but discretionary and dependent on market conditions; its sustainability is not assured as rates or markets move
findings.quote: The Council's Investment Strategy continued to perform well and the mix of longer-term multi-asset income funds and shorter-term money market investment both facilitated the operational needs of the Council and provided an income stream. The investments created a favourable variance of £165,000.

findings.headline: Pay award creating £71,000 budget overrun
findings.detail: The council's 3.3% pay award was approved and is now forecast to cost £71,000 above the original budget. Although not yet paid, it has been included in the forecast position.
findings.matters: Known payroll cost increases are a core indicator of budget sustainability for lenders and finance directors
findings.quote: it was forecast to cost £71,000 above budget. Although it was yet to be paid it had been included in the forecasts.
